Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
Supplementary affidavit filed today by the learned counsel for the applicant is taken on record.

2. Heard Sri Mukesh Kumar Pandey, learned counsel for the applicant as well as Ms. Ifra Islam,
learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material available on record.
3.
Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 282 of 2023, under Sections 366 & 376-D of I.P.C., Police Station - Sevarahi, District - Kushi Nagar, during the pendency of trial.

entities.text: Police Station - Sevarahi, District - Kushi Nagar

sentences.text:
PROSECUTION STORY:

1
4. The informant lodged the FIR alleging that he along with his wife met with an accident with a pickup vehicle on 16.07.2023 at about 10:00 PM when they were returning from a feast.
The persons travelling in the said pickup vehicle were three in number and they had abducted his wife and had taken her by the alleged pickup vehicle.
5. The said three unknown persons had outraged the modesty of his wife and left her near the house of the informant.

ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF APPLICANT:
6. The applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case due to ulterior motive.
He has nothing to do with the said offence as alleged in the FIR.
The applicant is not named in the FIR.
His name has come up during investigation on the basis of information received from a squealer by the police.
7. The FIR is delayed by seven hours and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.
The inordinate delay in lodging the FIR itself indicates that it is a case of false implication.

In the FIR,
there are allegations of abduction and outraging the modesty of the victim only but subsequently, as an improvement, the victim in her statement recorded u/s 161 & 164 Cr.P.C. has stated that she was raped.
The said allegation of rape has been made after legal consultation.
8. The victim has refused to get her internal medical examination and her external medical examination does not show any injury on her body.

9. The victim in her statement recorded u/s 164 Cr.P.C. and also during her statement recorded in Court has categorically stated that she suffered scratches on her back but the same does not find support by any medical evidence as no injury has been observed by the doctor conducting her medical examination.
10. The victim is stated to have met the applicant and other co-accused persons at a hospital whereby she is stated to have identified the applicant.
The said identification is not admissible in evidence as it is not as per the tenements of law.
11. The victim herein has for the first time identified the applicant and other co-accused persons in the doc at the time of examination-in-chief.
The said identification does not carry any force.

12. During her cross-examination, the victim has categorically stated that at the time of offence,
there was pitch dark, as such, she could not identify the assailants.
The said statement of the victim is self-contradictory.

13. The number of assailants have kept on increasing as initially, the assailants were supposed to be three persons but it has been increased to four persons at the stage of recording of statement of the victim.

Saddam vs State Of U.P. on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26820291/
2

14. Criminal history of three cases assigned to the applicant has been explained as in one case of the year 2016, he is on bail; another case is of police party firing wherein he himself has sustained injuries and the third case is under the Gangsters Act in which he was not found wanted.
15. Out of 29 prosecution witnesses, only seven witnesses have been examined till date.
There is no likelihood of applicant of tampering with the evidence as already the witnesses of fact have been examined.
16. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
17. The applicant is languishing in jail since 19.07.2023 and deserves to be released on bail.

In case,
the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and shall cooperate with trial.
ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF STATE:

18. The bail application has been opposed on the ground that the assailants have been increased from three to four persons but it does not have any force as at the time of offence, one of the assailants was driving the vehicle and he was not counted, thus, the victim has increased the number of assailants from three to four persons subsequently.

CONCLUSION:
19. In the case of Prabhakar Tewari Vs. State of U.P. and another, (2020) 11 SCC 648, the Supreme Court has observed that pendency of several criminal cases against an accused by itself cannot be a basis for refusal of bail.
20.

entities.text: Prabhakar Tewari Vs. State of U.P. and another, (2020) 11 SCC 648
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In so far as criminal antecedents of the applicant is concerned, it is not the case of the State that applicant might tamper with or otherwise adversely influence the investigation, or that he might intimidate witnesses before or during the trial.
The State has also not placed any material that applicant in past attempted to evade the process of law.

If the accused is otherwise found to be entitled to bail, he cannot be denied bail only on the ground of criminal history, no exceptional circumstances on the basis of criminal antecedents have been shown to deny bail to accused, hence,
the Court does not feel it proper to deny bail to the applicant just on the ground of criminal antecedent.
21. The well-known principle of "Presumption of Innocence Unless Proven Guilty," gives rise to the concept of bail as a rule and imprisonment as an exception.

22. A person's right to life and liberty, guaranteed by Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, cannot be taken away simply because the person is accused of committing an offence until the guilt is established beyond a reasonable doubt.

Article 21 of the Indian Constitution states that no one's life or personal liberty may be taken away unless the procedure established by law is followed, and the Saddam vs State Of U.P. on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26820291/
3 procedure must be just and reasonable.

The said principle has been reiterated by the Supreme Court in Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690.
23.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Reiterating the aforesaid view, the Supreme Court in the case of Manish Sisodia Vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595, has again emphasized that the very well-settled principle of law that bail is not to be withheld as a punishment is not to be forgotten.

entities.text: Manish Sisodia Vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is high time that the Courts should recognize the principle that "bail is a rule and jail is an exception".
24.
Learned AGA could not bring forth any exceptional circumstances which would warrant denial of bail to the applicant.
25. It is settled principle of law that the object of bail is to secure the attendance of the accused at the trial.

No material particulars or circumstances suggestive of the applicant fleeing from justice or thwarting the course of justice or creating other troubles in the shape of repeating offences or intimidating witnesses and the like have been shown by learned AGA.

26. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and taking into consideration the rival submissions and the fact that no proper identification parade of the applicant and other co-accused persons has been conducted coupled by the fact that the case is fixed for prosecution evidence as only seven prosecution witnesses have been examined out of 29, as such, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

27. Let the applicant- Saddam, who is involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
28. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.

29. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
Order Date:- 14.8.2024
Siddhant (Justice Krishan Pahal)
